extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance personnel, repair stations, and FAA certification offices responsible for compliance with airworthiness directives
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Aviation Administration airworthiness directives specifying required inspections, modifications, replacements, life-limits, compliance times, and procedures for specified aircraft models and components. The page lists actions to be performed, timing, acceptable service information, and administrative procedures for alternate compliance and special flight permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1.2 adjustment factor for Model 747SR compliance times
rubrics_metrics.description: For Model 747SR airplanes only, based on continued mixed operation of lower cabin differentials, the inspection and modification compliance times specified in this AD may be multiplied by a 1.2 adjustment factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies only to Model 747SR and only when continued mixed operation of lower cabin differentials exists; adjusts the compliance times in the AD by multiplying by 1.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate means of compliance (AMOC) approval — Seattle ACO
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for AMOC should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment, and then send it to the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding AMOC requests via FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment, and then send it to the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PMI acts as the initial FAA point of contact for AMOC requests and forwards with concurrence/comments to the appropriate Aircraft Certification Office manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits (FAR 21.197 / 21.199)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base in order to comply with the requirements of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may obtain limited flight authorization to move aircraft to a location where required maintenance/modifications can be performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boeing 767 compliance time (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance is required within the next 90 days after the effective date of this AD, unless previously accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must accomplish the specified actions within the 90-day window measured from the AD effective date unless already done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boeing 767 — Group 1: inspection and rework of acoustical seal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Group 1 airplanes, perform the inspection and rework of the acoustical seal for entry/service doors in accordance with paragraph III., Part B., of Boeing Service Bulletin 767-25-0123, dated May 25, 1989, or Revision 1, dated September 14, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced Boeing Service Bulletin paragraph and revision specified; service bulletin is listed as the acceptable source of procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boeing 767 — Group 2: rework acoustical seal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Group 2 airplanes, rework the acoustical seal for entry/service doors in accordance with paragraph in., Part C., of Boeing Service Bulletin 767-25-0123, dated May 25, 1989, or Revision 1, dated September 14, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced Boeing Service Bulletin paragraph and revision specified for Group 2 airplanes.

rubrics_metrics.name: BAe Jetstream compliance time (600 hours TIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance: Required within the next 600 hours time-in-service after the effective date of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The compliance interval is expressed in flight hours (time-in-service).

rubrics_metrics.name: BAe Jetstream — modify selector valve per ASB
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the emergency gear and flap extension hydraulic system selector valve as described in BAe Alert Service Bulletin Jetstream 29-A-JA-881143, dated February 24, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform the modification exactly as described in the BAe Alert Service Bulletin; the CAA-UK classified the ASB as mandatory for continued airworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: BAe Jetstream — AMOC approval via Brussels ACO
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate method of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an equivalent level of safety may be approved by the Manager, Brussels Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Europe, Africa, and Middle East Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be forwarded through an FAA Maintenance Inspector, who may add comments and send it to the Manager, Brussels ACO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessna — inspection schedule for main gear inner bearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the accumulation of 1,300 hours time-in-service (TIS), or within the next 300 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 1,000 hours TIS, inspect the left and right main gear strut barrel inner bearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes an initial inspection threshold and recurring inspection interval; operators must track TIS and comply accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessna — bearing inspection procedure (removal and visual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the appropriate Aircraft Service Manual or Maintenance Manual, remove the lower barrel and axle assemblies from the upper barrel assemblies; remove all oil and grease from external lock rings, inner ring bearings, and extended stop spacers; visually inspect the external lock rings, inner bearings, and extended stop spacers for cracks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the aircraft's service/maintenance manual for removal procedures, then perform thorough cleaning and visual inspection before proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessna — replacement criteria for cracked parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If any cracks are found in the external lock rings or the extended stop spacers, prior to further flight replace the cracked part with a serviceable part. If any cracks are found in the inner bearings, prior to further flight replace the cracked part with a Part Number (P/N) 5141109-1 bearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any cracked component must be replaced before the aircraft is flown again; specified replacement part number for inner bearings is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessna — magnetic particle non-destructive inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: If no cracks are found, magnetic particle inspect the inner bearings using the procedures specified in Part B, 'MAGNETIC PARTICLE NONDESTRUCTIVE INSPECTION PROCEDURES' of Cessna Service Bulletin MEB88-7, dated December 2, 1988. If any cracks are found, prior to further flight replace the cracked part with a P/N 5141109-1 bearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the referenced service bulletin's NDT procedures for magnetic particle inspection; replace any cracked bearings found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessna — terminating action: new bearing P/N 5141109-1
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1,000 hour repetitive inspections specified in paragraph (a) of this AD are no longer required when the P/N 5141109-1 bearing is installed in each gear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation of the redesigned (new) bearing is a terminating action for the repetitive inspection requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessna — AMOC approval via Wichita ACO
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate method of compliance or adjustment of the initial or repetitive compliance times which provides an equivalent level of safety may be approved by the Manager, Wichita Aircraft Certification Office, FAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be forwarded through an FAA Maintenance Inspector, who may add comments and send it to the Manager, Wichita ACO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — 1,200-hour service life limit for specified tail rotor gearboxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposes a 1,200-hour time-in-service life limit on tail rotor spiral miter gear-sets used on certain Enstrom model helicopters; gearboxes with 1,200 or more hours since last overhaul must be retired from service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The life limit is mandatory; operators must track hours since last overhaul and retire gearboxes that have reached or exceeded 1,200 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — immediate action within five hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the next five hours' time in service: determine from the aircraft log book if the specified tail rotor gearbox is installed; remove all -1, -3 or -5 tail rotor gearboxes containing the specified spiral miter gear-sets with 1,200 or more hours TIS since last overhaul and replace with an airworthy gearbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an urgent/short-notice compliance requirement to mitigate imminent safety risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — inspection for gearboxes with less than 1,200 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: For tail rotor gearboxes with less than 1,200 hours' time in service since the last overhaul, remove the magnetic chip detector (plug), drain the oil from the tail rotor gearbox, filter the oil using a white filter paper, and inspect the magnetic plug and the filter paper with a ten-power magnifying glass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform careful contamination inspection using white filter paper and a 10x magnifier as an initial screen for metal debris.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — contaminant thresholds requiring replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inspection reveals the presence of more than 15 thin metal flakes, splinters, or granular-shaped steel particles greater than 0.005-inches thick or longer than 0.015 inches, remove and replace the tail rotor gearbox with an airworthy gearbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides numeric thresholds for unacceptable contamination and mandatory replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — further servicing and serviceability check procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If contaminants are fewer/smaller than the threshold, flush the gearbox with clean oil, clean the magnetic plug with a cotton swab and/or air gun (do not use a strong magnet), refill with specified lubricants, conduct a serviceability check by flying the helicopter for one hour at various power settings up to full power, and then repeat the inspection; if any contaminants are found on repeat, replace the gearbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes stepwise remediation: flush/clean, refill with approved lubricants, test flight, and re-inspect; any contaminants on repeat inspection mandate replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — prohibition on cleaning magnetic plug with strong magnet
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: Do not clean the magnetic plug with a strong magnet. This weakens the magnet on the chip detector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: using a strong magnet to clean the detector is prohibited because it degrades detector performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — lubricant specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Refill the tail rotor gearbox with Mil-L-6082B Shell SAE10W, Mil-L-6082B Texaco SAE10W, or Mil-L-22851B Phillips SAE 20W-50W lubricant. If any of these lubricants are not available, consult Enstrom Helicopter Corporation, Customer Service Department, for a possible alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must use one of the specified lubricants or seek manufacturer guidance for acceptable substitutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — recurring 100-hour inspection interval
rubrics_metrics.description: At intervals not to exceed 100 hours' time in service on all gearboxes returned to service after passing the initial inspections, remove the magnetic chip detector (plug), drain the oil, filter the oil using a white filter paper, and inspect the magnetic plug and filter paper with a ten-power magnifying glass. If any metal contaminants are found, remove and replace the tail rotor gearbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a recurring monitoring interval and replacement-on-contamination policy for in-service gearboxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — removal and replacement at 1,200 hours since last overhaul
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 1,200 hours' time in service since the last overhaul, remove and replace the tail rotor gearbox with an airworthy gearbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory retirement action at the service life limit regardless of inspection findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enstrom — AMOC approval and flight-to-base allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate method of compliance with this AD, which provides an equivalent level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Chicago Aircraft Certification Office. In accordance with Sections 21.197 and 21.199, flight is permitted to a base where the maintenance required by this AD may be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMOC requests addressed to Chicago ACO; special flight permits permissible to reach maintenance location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airbus A300 — repetitive inspections for disbonding and corrosion
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires repetitive inspections for disbonding and corrosion of certain structural components identified by full-scale fatigue testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections are recurring and prompted by fatigue-test-identified susceptible areas; documentation and service information from Airbus referenced for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airbus A300 — eddy current and ultrasonic inspections of fuselage lap joints
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires eddy current and ultrasonic inspections of the fuselage longitudinal lap joints for cracks, and repair, if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NDT methods (eddy current and ultrasonic) on longitudinal lap joints; perform repairs where cracks are found per applicable service/repair procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airbus A300 — area-specific clarification (Sections 13 and 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph B of the final rule was clarified to indicate that if no disbonding or corrosion is found in areas other than Section 13 and 14, no further action is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inspection finds no disbonding/corrosion outside the identified critical sections, the operator need not take additional action beyond the specified inspections.
